Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we have Diego and Priya on the call. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan: good thanks, morning from NY. we've got a packed agenda so appreciate you fitting this in.
[00:13] Tara: hey, thanks. we've had a few spikes in the last week so wanted to do a health pulse with you all.
[00:20] Diego: great, we'll share what we've seen on our side, and then dig into the dedicated options and the VPC/onprem timeline. disclaimer: some of the names in the transcript may be off, apologies if i mispronounce anything.

[00:45] Maya: quick high level: Aurea has been using Redwood Hosted for the last 9 weeks under the pilot, chat generation plus embeddings. traffic up about 2.7x last month per your dashboard, Priya do you want to pull the exact numbers?
[00:56] Priya: yeah, so monthly token count is ~42M tokens, embeddings calls are about 18% of calls, chat generation approx 60% and the rest are tokenized rerank requests. there's a daily peak at 10am PST that accounts for 28% of daily traffic.
[01:12] Jordan: correct. the peak was partly due to a marketing test, and then it stuck so we've got more steady traffic now.

[01:35] Tara: cost is our top question; the last invoice had a big delta. we want to understand what drove the increase and what it would look like on dedicated.
[01:44] Maya: totally. the main drivers we see are the increase in sequence length on chat completions and some unbatched embedding calls. also, a few very long context requests hit the P99 token length. we can break that down.
[01:55] Devon: quick clarification — when you say sequence length distribution, is that the window size of the model or the prompt length?
[02:02] Diego: both are related; prompt length drives tokens to generate, and runtime kernel selection is sensitive to peak sequence lengths. for example, if you jump from 512 to 2k frequently, that pushes you into different execution paths.

[02:25] Jordan: are there quick fixes? like prefix caching, or we could precompute some embeddings?
[02:30] Diego: yes — prefix/KV cache helps for repeated context; for embeddings we recommend batching small requests and using a lightweight embedding model for search index updates. also quantization profiles can reduce per-token GPU cost on Dedicated.

[03:05] Tara: walk me through Dedicated vs Hosted for our use case. we care about predictable throughput and data isolation, but also don't want to overcommit.
[03:12] Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and predictable billing; Hosted is pay-as-you-go but can have variability during spikes. Redwood Dedicated also supports private VPC peering and customer-managed keys.
[03:27] Jordan: how quick is a canary or rollback? we do frequent model rollouts.
[03:32] Diego: rollouts are handled by the console with canaries and A/B; if you pin versions you can do gradual traffic shift. rollback is usually near-instant but cache warmup may cause temporary latency differences.

[03:58] Speaker 1: (unclear) can we see an example of the latency impact when we enable KV caching?
[04:02] Diego: yes, we have a shared spreadsheet with sample runs. i'll run a KV cache on your sample session and show P50/P95 delta.

[04:33] Tara: on security, are you SOC 2 Type II and do you have customer KMS integration? we need details for procurement.
[04:40] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 certified, we'll share the report, plus the network diagram. for KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys in supported clouds and HSM for private deployments. note: some of the compliance docs are behind NDA but we'll surface what we can.

[05:05] Jordan: any gotchas for data residency? we need EU region hosting for some clients.
[05:11] Diego: we can pin regions; for Dedicated we can reserve capacity in eu-west-1 or related regions. for on-prem it's also possible but takes extra lead time.

[05:30] Devon: timeline question: if we decide to go Dedicated, how long to provision?
[05:34] Maya: standard lead time for Reserved Dedicated is 4-6 weeks after contract, earlier if we have capacity in region. Private/onprem can be 6-12 weeks depending on network and security review.

[06:01] Tara: cost modeling: can you show hosted vs dedicated break-even?
[06:06] Maya: yes, i'll prepare a three-tier pricing scenario: pure hosted forecast, small dedicated pool with autoscale for bursts, and full dedicated with committed monthly. that'll include unit economics at current token mix.

[06:30] Jordan: also, curious on fallback policies — if dedicated pool is saturated, what's the behaviour?
[06:35] Diego: policy-based routing can failover to compatible model variants in hosted region or enqueue with priority. fallback can be configured per route: degrade quality (smaller model) or increase latency with queued requests.

[06:58] Tara: for benchmarking, we'd like to run a 48-hour stress test with representative queries and simultaneous sessions to observe tail latency and KV cache effect. can Redwood run that in your staging environment?
[07:08] Diego: yes, we can run controlled stress tests; we'll need your sample workload and API keys scoped for the test. we'll provide a runbook and an analysis template.

[07:28] Priya: i'll put the template in the shared folder. link: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-deck/aurea (note: internal link, need access rights).

[07:45] Jordan: a couple of operational items: on-call runbooks, error alerts thresholds, and cost alerts. do you have built-in dashboards we can plug into?
[07:54] Maya: Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency dashboards, and trace hooks. we can enable alerting on P95 latency and cost burn rate.

[08:18] Tara: on a smaller note: we're evaluating SAML SSO for your console and want RBAC integration with our IdP.
[08:24] Diego: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, plus role-based access controls. we'll share the SAML metadata and a sample SCIM JSON.

[08:50] Jordan: competitor question — we looked at Anthropic and Vertex for price, any significant technical differences we should watch for?
[08:57] Maya: main diffs are pricing model and operational tooling; Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. others might have different batching/latency tradeoffs. we'll send a comparison doc.

[09:20] Devon: if we go with dedicated, can we bring custom plugin modules or local tokenizers?
[09:26] Diego: on Dedicated we support some customizations; plugin support depends on the model and security posture. local tokenizers are possible on Private/on-prem deployments but need validation.

[09:50] Speaker 2: (mumble) do you have per-route throttles?
[09:53] Priya: yes per-route quotas and rate limits, plus token-based quotas.

[10:10] Tara: about long context windows — we've got a feature with 8k context for some customers. how does that affect pricing and perf?
[10:18] Diego: long context increases memory and KV cache size; it changes kernel selection and can increase P95. for cost we model per token rendered plus memory footprint — we'll include a scenario for 8k contexts.

[10:45] Jordan: can we get a breakdown of the last incident — there was a 15 minute latency spike two Tuesdays ago.
[10:51] Maya: yes, we pulled traces; it was due to a sudden XY load combined with a misconfigured autoscale signal in your routing policy, plus a small KV cache eviction storm. we'll attach the postmortem.

[11:13] Tara: what mitigations do you suggest?
[11:16] Diego: tune autoscale signal to use longer smoothing windows, enable reserve headroom for critical routes, and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.

[11:40] Jordan: procurement path: we need a PO checklist, SOC2, contract terms around data retention and deletion.
[11:46] Priya: Priya here — i'll produce a checklist and the standard contract redlines we usually accept.

[12:05] Devon: question about KV cache — is that customer-specific or shared across tenants?
[12:10] Diego: caches are per-tenant in Dedicated and isolated; hosted uses logical separation and does per-tenant KV namespaces.

[12:32] Jordan: any recommended quantization profiles? we've seen odd hallucination regressions when we tried 4-bit quantization.
[12:39] Diego: yep, quantization can impact generation fidelity. we have validated quant profiles per model; for chat we'd suggest mixed precision or per-layer calibrations. our Optimize team can run a quick eval set.

[13:05] Tara: we're also evaluating a mid-Nov pilot ramp to 3x traffic — do you see capacity risk?
[13:11] Maya: at current token mix, hosted should handle the ramp but costs will increase; for predictability you might reserve a small dedicated pool and use burst autoscale. we'll simulate the ramp in the perf test.

[13:35] Jordan: is there a penalty on Dedicated if we need to downsize after contract?
[13:40] Maya: contracts typically have a term and adjustment provisions; we can negotiate a step-down plan in the SOW. Priya will draft typical clauses.

[13:55] Tara: ok, let's recap next steps.
[13:58] Maya: recap: 1) Maya shares three-tier pricing and cost breakdown by 2026-10-05; 2) Diego runs 48h stress test in staging using your sample traffic and shares results by 2026-10-06; 3) Tara uploads traffic histograms by 2026-10-04; 4) Priya drafts PO/contract checklist by 2026-10-08 and attaches SOC2 + network diagram; 5) schedule on-prem deep-dive week of 2026-10-11 if you want to pursue Private. correct?
[14:20] Jordan: yes that's accurate. thank you.
[14:23] Devon: one last ask — can we get a quick note on model variant fallbacks (which models are compatible) so we can design client logic?
[14:29] Diego: yes i'll include a compatibility matrix.

[14:45] Priya: i'll send calendar invites for the perf run kickoff and the on-prem deep-dive.

[14:58] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email with artifacts.
[15:02] Jordan: thanks all, great sync.
